attempts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a fresh Crooktail character study sheet as a Canadian Group of Seven oil study folio. The result must look painted by the SAME hand as the FIRST TWO landscape references, with their organization of colour, light and brushwork.

REFERENCE HIERARCHY
Image 1, the apple-orchard hillside: PRIMARY reference for flowing brush rhythm, simplified connected colour masses, matte oil colour, sky-filled light and selective edges.
Image 2, the stream-after-ash landscape: PRIMARY reference for grey/green/blue-violet harmonies, connected shadow masses and broad rock/tree form.

PAINTING AND LIGHT
Canadian Group of Seven, with the rhythmic form and expressive colour relationships of A. Y. Jackson. Build the animal as large, flowing, interlocking shapes, like the rocks and hills in the reference paintings. The overall light/shadow pattern must read before any texture.
Broad, assured opaque oil brushstrokes curve around the haunches, sweep along back and tail, and gather into larger muzzle and paw planes. Thick paint belongs to deliberate strokes and selective accents. Retain quiet passages and varied stroke widths. Show a few scumbled or scraped joins, never a uniform armour of thousands of lifted flakes.
Use soft northern sky light: broad slate-blue illumination over the upper back, a connected deep indigo/umber shadow below, subdued moss reflections on the underside. In every study, this is the SAME diffuse natural light, not a separately spotlit specimen. The face is part of that light mass. Eyes and nose are simple dark painted notes. No glowing eyes, pinpoint glassy catchlights, gold rim light, cinematic orange/teal grading, studio key light, metallic edge glitter, bloom or 3D bevel shading on each brushstroke.
Keep the animal dark-furred and substantial, with charcoal, muted indigo, brown-black and restrained grey-violet light. Colour is expressive but never metallic. Both body AND head should be as simplified and painterly as the landscape's trees/rocks; don't leave a realistic face inside a coarse body.
The ground is quiet warm ivory with lightly brushed opaque oil, NOT thick frosting. No sharp shiny plaster relief across the blank page.

IDENTITY
One physical furred, nonverbal four-legged beast. Broad muzzle, small rounded ears, ordinary dark eyes, a long tail with a single true right-angle bend UP near its end, and a thin pale seam on the LEFT forepaw. All views must agree. Fur is real, not smoke. No added wings/horns/human traits. The separate 'After rescue' study shows a narrow wrapping band of rubbed fur around the hindquarters; keep intact fur in other studies.

SHEET
Landscape 1536x1024, generous ivory spacing. Readable dark serif heading "CROOKTAIL" and title "Friends of the Night", restrained in scale, with generous spacing. Two or three uncropped useful body views, one simplified head study, a paw study and separate after-rescue hindquarter study. Useful exact labels: "Lateral", "Wary", "Rear", "Pale forepaw seam", "After rescue". No extra prose.
Bottom: a compact vignette approaching a flat eel-stone under hazels beside a stream, with TWO eels. Use gentle fading daylight under a pale blue-grey sky, without an orange sunset spotlight. The animal must belong to the same light and brushwork as its setting. Finish with a small palette strip.
This is an expressive oil painter's field-study page, not fantasy game concept art, a glossy render with impasto pasted on it, mosaic, carved wood, encrusted chips, photorealism or digital illustration.
